private lot and hit him. unit 2 stated that he had his hands on the hood and was knocked off the side of the truck. i did not observe any reflective gear on unit 2, which it was still dark outside at the time of the accident. i then spoke with d1 of unit 1. d1 stated he [roadway]. d1 stated he was waiting to turn into the [roadway] way. d1 stated that two cars pulled into the private lot and he followed behind them. d1 stated he then heard noise around the passenger front side of his vehicle and that is when he saw d2 on top of the vehicle from the side, not on the front. d2 then waited to make sure d2 was okay and waited at the incident scene. d1 did state to me that he did not see d2. i then contacted a gap detective. i spoke with det. warren #2365 and i relayed [case id]. det. warren advised me to right the following report with no suspects, as of now, it seemed unit 2(pedestrian) was at fault due to unit 2 hitting the side of the truck, possibly meaning that unit 1 was more than records.deidentified_narrative: unit 1 was traveling east in the [roadway]. unit 1 attempted to turn right onto the [roadway]. several witnesses stated the light was green and unit 1 came to a stop before turning right. unit 1 struck the pedestrian causing the pedestrian to fall to the ground. the pedestrian was taken to houston methodist clear lake by seabrook medic 10 for minor injuries. after further investigation, it was determined the victim's husband, (coggeshall, john), stated he pushed the crosswalk button. john also stated the white crosswalk symbol turned on before his wife and him entered the crosswalk. unit 1 driver stated his light was green as he approached the intersection to turn right. unit 1 driver also stated when he looked up, the crosswalk red hand was displayed. unit 1 passenger stated she was putting on makeup using the passenger side visor mirror. with the unit 1 passenger leaned forward with the passenger side mirror down, this may have created a blind spot for the unit 1 driver. unit 1 passenger also stated she saw a red hand symbol on the crosswalk sign for do not cross. all witnesses stated they saw a green light but could not recall what crosswalk symbol was displayed. sergeant oubre and i went to the intersection to watch the light cycle and the crosswalk with the button being pushed and the button not being pushed several times. when the crosswalk button is not pushed, it never gives the white symbol displaying for pedestrians to cross. when the crosswalk button is pushed, the white symbol allowing pedestrians to cross is displayed for a few seconds while the intersection light is red heading [roadway]. when the intersection light turns green for east bound traffic, the white symbol is displayed for a few seconds then turns back to the red hand for do not cross with the timer displaying 0. officers were unable to determine what pedestrians' symbol was displayed for the crosswalk due to conflicting stories.

records.public_safe_text: unit 1 was traveling east in the [roadway]. unit 1 attempted to turn right onto the [roadway]. several witnesses stated the light was green and unit 1 came to a stop before turning right. unit 1 struck the pedestrian causing the pedestrian to fall to the ground. the pedestrian was taken to houston methodist clear lake by seabrook medic 10 for minor injuries. after further investigation, it was determined the victim's husband, (coggeshall, john), stated he pushed the crosswalk button. john also stated the white crosswalk symbol turned on before his wife and him entered the crosswalk. unit 1 driver stated his light was green as he approached the intersection to turn right. unit 1 driver also stated when he looked up, the crosswalk red hand was displayed. unit 1 passenger stated she was putting on makeup using the passenger side visor mirror. with the unit 1 passenger leaned forward with the passenger side mirror down, this may have created a blind spot for the unit 1 driver. unit 1 passenger also stated she saw a red hand symbol on the crosswalk sign for do not cross. all witnesses stated they saw a green light but could not recall what crosswalk symbol was displayed. sergeant oubre and i went to the intersection to watch the light cycle and the crosswalk with the button being pushed and the button not being pushed several times. when the crosswalk button is not pushed, it never gives the white symbol displaying for pedestrians to cross. when the crosswalk button is pushed, the white symbol allowing pedestrians to cross is displayed for a few seconds while the intersection light is red heading [roadway]. when the intersection light turns green for east bound traffic, the white symbol is displayed for a few seconds then turns back to the red hand for do not cross with the timer displaying 0. officers were unable to determine what pedestrians' symbol was displayed for the crosswalk due to conflicting stories.
